windowsHandleTransition: Keep the current read/share-READ deny-write/delete candidate handle and held ancestors. Open a READ witness with share-READ|DELETE and OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, and compare volume/file index, exact length, regular type, no reparse and single link to the original. This does not permit writes while either handle exists.

Only after that witness is held, drop the original deny-delete handle. Open the same exact candidate with READ|DELETE access and share-READ only, again compare identity/length and current fixed path to the witness. The witness prevents writes through this transition; the new handle now denies other writers and deleters. A replacement or failed open rejects without renaming the replacement. No unlock-then-fs::rename fallback.

Retain this READ|DELETE/share-READ handle through rename, rehash and journal commit. Rename its exact object via bounded FILE_RENAME_INFO to the internally derived same-job media.mp4 with ReplaceIfExists=false. All ancestors remain pinned and checked. Use the existing fixed absolute-name handle-rename pattern; no arbitrary path or recursive operation. Destination collision is an error, never overwrite.

After rename, inspect the fixed media.mp4 path using a compatible read-attributes handle that shares the held DELETE access; compare exact identity/length and full expected hash. Do not close the owning handle merely to reopen a legacy GuardedFile. The finalizer already synced candidate payload before verification; do not claim a new FlushFileBuffers guarantee from a read-only handle. Rename success plus durable job journal is the application commit, not a guarantee against all filesystem/power-loss behavior.

If failure occurs before rename, retain the merge candidate; after rename, retain media.mp4 and the last truthful journal. Do not rename back, search for a moved file, delete, truncate or overwrite anything. A later recovery must reconstruct proof, not treat media.mp4 existence as success. Non-Windows behavior remains unsupported until an equally strict implementation is separately verified.
serviceOwnership: Keep existing JobOwnership alive for the entire worker. Match provider YouTube/live, job/request/video/broadcast, exact download root and the complete receiver/source/document/generation/RecordingOwner identity against expected and candidate. A scheduled owner includes run, generation, canonical channel and exact video; do not check a newer currently running broadcast in place of the old file's immutable owner.

Under the existing state mutex, require current cancellation Arc::ptr_eq, current observed revision, active verifying/finalizing state, no library entry and no shutdown/cancel. Every owned phase update persists its cloned job before replacing memory and advances the expected revision. Do not use blind update for the new branch. Reject a retry/replacement owner even if the job ID is reused.

Reuse current bounded verification semaphore, duration/full-decode checks, optional poster, chat-status recovery and LibraryItem field construction. Keep all candidate/source guards during external reads and honor the original absolute deadline rather than giving each stage a fresh24hours. Existing general checks supplement, never replace, the stronger native admission and exact packet proof.

Recheck CAS immediately before short handle rename under state lock. Perform final hash/poster/chat work outside that lock. Reacquire it, recheck installed file/source guards and exact owner/cancel/revision, then durably save completed+LibraryItem and replace memory while keeping the installed handle. Service cancel/shutdown serialize on this same mutex; any additional unsynchronized cancellation writer must be audited before integration rather than assumed atomic with commit.

Cancellation, owner change, timeout or journal failure after rename leaves the file retained without a new completed/library success. Reuse the existing terminal persistence-error latch and last-journal preservation. Do not remove cancel ownership until the actual worker finishes. Chat partial/unavailable state remains truthful and its original records remain; video success must not rewrite chat to complete.
